title: Initialize active feature planning ledger
decision: Use `pldg-20260626-001-feature-name` as the active v2 Bootstrap Planning Ledger for the exact placeholder feature token `<feature name>`. The ledger is source/planning memory only; canonical Plans and generated governance/build artifacts remain untouched until explicit compile or governance-seal permission is given.

title: Start miscellaneous PM history surfaces with documents and runs
decision: The first miscellaneous PM item is to let users see historical documents made by the wizard, specifically Plans and PRD docs created by the wizard, and historical Orchestrator runs in PM. The feature requires GUI design and likely routes through the Orchestrator page. This does not authorize canonical Plans edits, PlanUnit indexes, WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, Spec_Lock, shards, evidence, plan_graph, or auto_decisions.

title: Accept History defaults and full run action scope
decision: Historical wizard documents default to final/approved outputs, with a user expansion control to show everything. Historical Orchestrator runs support all proposed actions: view/search/filter, open artifacts/evidence, resume/retry where valid, clone as a new run, export, and inspect Ledger/raw records. The GUI home is the existing Orchestrator History tab with Documents and Runs views or equivalent subviews. Resume/retry/clone actions must create or bind current live continuations and must not mutate immutable historical records in place. This does not authorize canonical Plans edits, PlanUnit indexes, WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, Spec_Lock, shards, evidence, plan_graph, or auto_decisions.

title: Accept current-project lock, retention defaults, and document-specific actions
decision: Orchestrator History is locked to the current project. Final/approved wizard outputs are retained forever by default and stay visible in the default Documents view. Drafts, intermediate outputs, previous non-final versions, and other all-history rows can be archive/retention governed while remaining discoverable through expanded all-history when retained. Document rows use document-specific actions: Open, Compare versions, Duplicate as draft, Reopen in Wizard, Export, and Send forward when currentness allows. Send-forward and reopen actions require currentness and authority checks and must not mutate immutable historical records in place. This does not authorize canonical Plans edits, PlanUnit indexes, WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, Spec_Lock, shards, evidence, plan_graph, or auto_decisions.

title: Accept dense History rows, Approved/All control, and deep comparison MVP
decision: Orchestrator History uses dense table columns by default: Name, Type, Status, Version, Created/Approved, Source, Last action, and Artifacts. The Documents view uses a simple current-project `Approved only` versus `All history` control/chip. `Compare versions` requires deep comparison in MVP, including rendered output, package/source-lineage metadata, source ledger atom lineage where applicable, and package/manifest identity; deeper comparison is not deferred. Export granularity remains open. This does not authorize canonical Plans edits, PlanUnit indexes, WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, Spec_Lock, shards, evidence, plan_graph, or auto_decisions.

title: Accept all History export granularities in MVP
decision: History export supports all proposed MVP granularities: selected-row export, multi-select bundle export, and whole current filtered-view export with an identity-preserving manifest. Export manifests must preserve canonical object identities and refs for rows, documents, runs, artifacts, evidence, lineage, active filters, and current-project scope. Export formats/profiles remain open. This does not authorize canonical Plans edits, PlanUnit indexes, WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, Spec_Lock, shards, evidence, plan_graph, or auto_decisions.

title: Accept export profiles, comparison layout, and archived visibility
decision: History export MVP supports archive/zip with manifest, JSON, rendered Markdown, rendered HTML, and rendered PDF. Raw records and evidence can be included only through an explicit evidence/redaction profile selected by the user, not silently in ordinary rendered exports. Deep document comparison uses a combined comparison view with side-by-side rendered diff, metadata/source-lineage pane, and atom/manifest change table. Archived records appear only after an extra `Include archived` control inside All history and must remain visibly marked as archived when shown. The History source-of-truth/indexing contract remains open. This does not authorize canonical Plans edits, PlanUnit indexes, WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, Spec_Lock, shards, evidence, plan_graph, or auto_decisions.

title: Accept unified project History projection
decision: History uses a project-scoped unified History index/projection as its read model instead of direct ad hoc queries across each subsystem at view time. The projection preserves canonical identities and references immutable source records for wizard documents, Orchestrator runs, artifacts, evidence, source lineage, package manifests, and archive state; it must not become the mutable authority for those objects. History UI behaviors, filters, exports, compare entry points, archive visibility, and artifact/evidence affordances read from the projection while resolving preserved source refs when opening, exporting, or performing authority/currentness-gated actions. Projection lifecycle and rebuild semantics remain open. This does not authorize canonical Plans edits, PlanUnit indexes, WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, Spec_Lock, shards, evidence, plan_graph, or auto_decisions.

title: Accept rebuildable event-updated History projection
decision: The unified History projection is rebuildable from immutable source records and updated by wizard save/approval, run lifecycle, artifact/evidence write, archive/unarchive, and lineage/manifest events. Stale, corrupt, incomplete, or out-of-sync projection state must be detected and surfaced in the History UI rather than silently driving rows, filters, exports, or compare flows. Rebuild and stale-state detection preserve immutable source identities and must not rewrite source history or mutate approved/final outputs in place. Degraded-mode action availability remains open. This does not authorize canonical Plans edits, PlanUnit indexes, WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, Spec_Lock, shards, evidence, plan_graph, or auto_decisions.

title: Accept stale History degraded-mode behavior
decision: When the History projection is stale or out-of-sync, the UI allows read-only viewing with a visible warning, exposes a user-visible `Rebuild` action, and blocks compare, export, reopen, and send-forward until rebuild succeeds. After successful rebuild, normal History actions may resume only subject to existing currentness, authority, retention, archive, and identity-preservation rules. A pre-compile readiness pressure-test remains open for the first miscellaneous History item. This does not authorize canonical Plans edits, PlanUnit indexes, WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, Spec_Lock, shards, evidence, plan_graph, or auto_decisions.

decision: Accept the pressure-test MVP defaults bundle for the first miscellaneous History item: exact History row schema fields, permissions/redaction export profile details, structured filter-chip search plus text search, explicit empty/degraded states, and acceptance-test coverage. title: Begin PM vision bridge planning from opencode-see-image reference
decision: Begin planning a PM-native adaptation of the `opencode-see-image` pattern for `models models without vision`. The external repo is useful as source-lineage for the capability shape: a `see_image` tool, prompt guidance to avoid guessing, image/screenshot resolution, and a vision-capable route that returns text to the non-vision model. The PM plan must adapt the pattern rather than install or depend on the OpenCode plugin implementation, OpenCode auth/database/CLI surfaces, Bun runtime, or OpenCode-specific default providers/models. Candidate decisions remain open for automatic fallback behavior, provider routing, PM-owned image sources, artifacts/cache, permissions/privacy, and GUI surfacing. This does not authorize canonical Plans edits, PlanUnit indexes, WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, Spec_Lock, shards, evidence, plan_graph, or auto_decisions.
